items.note: Aggregate placeholder for webbing, water, rations and small kit until M2.5 itemises it; rifle, magazines, helmet and vest are separate items.
Empty magazine mass published. See docs/research/ballistics.md (values from search extracts of the cited pages).
Helmet mass from the published 1.4 kg requirement; protection against fragments and pistol rounds (game value: 2.5 mm steel equivalent, so square rifle hits penetrate). See docs/research/squads.md.

Hard plates class SK4 (rifle rounds up to 7.62x51) front and back, soft armour SK1 around them. Mass is an estimate (not found); plate coverage of the chest is a game value. See docs/research/squads.md.

Under-barrel 40 mm grenade launcher, about 1.5 kg. The search tool declined these look-ups in the research session; values are from general published references as remembered and must be verified against a public source. Game abstraction.
120-round belt in a soft pouch; links counted in the belt mass; every fifth round tracer. Belt length and pouch mass are game values. Links counted in the empty mass.
20-round polymer magazine (published); mass estimated.
Panzerfaust 3 firing unit with sight, 2.3 kg (search extracts); kept after a shot, it takes the next round (de-pzf3-dm12, a 12.9 kg tube). Firing unit and one round: 15.2 kg as before M7.4a.

Two litres of water in canteens or a bladder (M11.6: a charged item, charge in ml; 2000 ml full). The 1.6 kg of the full item is kept: 0.8 g per ml folds the canteens into the water (water is 1 g/ml; empty canteens ~0.1-0.15 kg each, unsourced estimate): low, owner to review.
One day of rations. Mass is a typical value, not sourced; part of the itemised load that replaces the placeholder.

The pouch of the individual first-aid kit; its contents are counted items since M10.1 (one CAT tourniquet, two field dressings, haemostatic gauze, a rescue blanket, pain tablets: 0.6 kg with the pouch, the old placeholder mass). Official contents not found in search extracts (research 2026-11-14); typical values.
Load-carrying vest or belt kit, pouches, small pack, weather clothing, tools. Mass is a typical value, not sourced; part of the itemised load that replaces the placeholder.

Night-vision goggle; used by sensors in M9. Mass is a typical value, not sourced; part of the itemised load that replaces the placeholder. M11.6 power: 50 h on one AA (Thales Lucie 60 h at 1.5 V, PVS-14 class 40-50 h; search extracts, medium; 50 h chosen, low); 20 s to change the cell (inferred, low); switched on below light 0.5, the night sensor's nightLight, so it is on whenever it helps (review fix 2026-11-16; game value, low). Mass 0.585 kg without the cell (0.6 kg with it, as before).
M11.6: one AA lithium cell for the night-vision goggle; charge in Wh (Energizer L91: ~3.5 Ah at 1.5 V ~ 4-5 Wh, 15 g; mass medium, Wh rounded down to an integer 4: low, owner to review).

Section radio, typical mass (0.9 kg with its battery). M11.6 power: 6 h on a battery pack (SOVERON HR short pack, R&S datasheet search extract: medium); 10 s to change it (inferred, low). The battery is a separate item now: mass 0.55 kg without it (0.9 kg with it, as before).

M11.6: battery pack of the section handheld radio (SOVERON HR / SEM 52 SL class); charge in Wh. The R&S SOVERON HR datasheet gives up to 6 h on the short pack and more than 12 h on the long pack (search extract, duty cycle not stated): the radio's power.hours is 6 (short pack, medium). Capacity ~30 Wh and mass 0.35 kg are inferred from handheld packs (R-187P1: 466 g bare, ~900 g with battery and antenna; PRC-152 class 0.3-0.4 kg): low, owner to review.
30-round STANAG-type magazine for the G95A1; mass typical, not sourced.
The Puma's fuel tank (M7): the charge is litres of diesel (0.84 kg per litre). The tank itself is part of the hull (mass 0). Capacity is a game value.
Ready or stowed belt of 100 armour-piercing 30 mm rounds (Puma: 200 ready in two feeds and as many stowed are game values for the published total).
Ready or stowed belt of 100 high-explosive 30 mm rounds (split of the published total is a game value).
500-round belt for the coaxial MG5, every fifth round tracer (game values).
Game value: one charge of the vehicle's fire extinguishing system (M7.4b).

Combat Application Tourniquet type: every Bundeswehr soldier on operations carries at least one tourniquet (bundeswehr.de 'T-Tourniquet', search extract). About 80 g. The reference tourniquet (time and success factor 1).
Verbandpaeckchen / emergency (Israeli) pressure bandage. Game-value mass (typical commercial item); research 2026-11-14 from search extracts only.
Haemostatic gauze for wound packing (commercial EH-A sets, search extract). Game-value mass (typical commercial item); research 2026-11-14 from search extracts only.
Rescue blanket against hypothermia. Game-value mass (typical commercial item); research 2026-11-14 from search extracts only.
Tablet pack (TCCC style meloxicam and paracetamol). Game-value mass (typical commercial item); research 2026-11-14 from search extracts only.
Vented chest seal (first responder and medic bags). Game-value mass (typical commercial item); research 2026-11-14 from search extracts only.
Nasopharyngeal airway; Einsatzersthelfer B trains airway care (bundeswehr.de, search extract). Game-value mass (typical commercial item); research 2026-11-14 from search extracts only.
Needle for chest decompression (owner Q-1b: Einsatzersthelfer B may relieve the airway / chest). Game-value mass (typical commercial item); research 2026-11-14 from search extracts only.

Cannula and giving set; Einsatzersthelfer B trains IV access (bundeswehr.de 'Ausbildung Einsatzersthelfer Bravo', search extract). Game-value mass (typical commercial item); research 2026-11-14 from search extracts only.
Intra-osseous access (FAST1 / EZ-IO type), medics only. Game-value mass (typical commercial item); research 2026-11-14 from search extracts only.
500 ml crystalloid bag. Game-value mass (typical commercial item); research 2026-11-14 from search extracts only.
Ketamine for pain, medics only (TCCC). Game-value mass (typical commercial item); research 2026-11-14 from search extracts only.
SAM-type splint (about 115 g). Game-value mass (typical commercial item); research 2026-11-14 from search extracts only.

The Einsatzersthelfer B bag, empty; its contents are counted items in the man's load (two tourniquets, two haemostatic gauzes, four dressings, two chest seals, two nasal airways, a decompression needle, an IV set and two 500 ml bags, pain tablets, two rescue blankets, a splint: about 3 kg). Official contents not found (research 2026-11-14); proposal.

The Sanitaeter's bag, empty; contents as the first responder's bag plus an IO set, ketamine and more dressings (bundeswehr.de 'Erster am Verwundeten: der Medic', search extract; quantities a proposal).

Folding litter (faltbare Trage) carried by the Sanitaeter (research 2026-11-14: bundeswehr.de 'Erster am Verwundeten: der Medic', search extract, lists a litter in the medic's kit). Mass a game value (folding NATO-pattern litters weigh about 6-7 kg). Used by a four-man stretcher carry (M10.4a); not used up.
Red cross armband: marks the wearer as medical personnel (GC I art. 40). Worn by the Sanitaeter (owner answer 6: marked medics are protected while not fighting).
The Boxer's fuel tank (M10.6-data): the charge is litres of diesel (0.84 kg per litre); 562 L as commonly quoted (search extracts). The tank is part of the hull (mass 0).
Game value: one charge of the vehicle's fire extinguishing system.

Thermal weapon sight (M9.2): IdZ-ES optics include a combined reflex and thermal rifle sight (Thales XTRAIM, search extracts); how many a Gruppe has is not public. Research default, low (owner round M9 screen 3 (a)): one per Schuetzentrupp, with the marksman. Mass is a game value. M11.6 power: 7 h on 3x AA (Hensoldt IRV-MR >= 7 h at 21 C, datasheet search extract, medium); 15 s to change the set (IRV-MR 'quick, blind battery replacement'; seconds inferred, low); always on (it magnifies and sees heat by day too, so it drains by day: review fix 2026-11-16; game value, low). Mass 0.855 kg without the cells (0.9 kg with them, as before).
M11.6: a set of 3 AA lithium cells for the clip-on thermal sight (Hensoldt IRV-MR runs on 3x AA, >= 7 h at 21 C; search extract); charge in Wh (3 x ~4 Wh, 3 x 15 g). Low, owner to review.
Thermal (multispectral) camouflage blanket (M9.2): a still man under it shows a quarter of his heat to a thermal sight. Game values; not issued to anyone by default (no public per-squad issue found).
One Spike LR missile in its canister for MELLS (M9.3a). Canister mass is a game value.

Bundeswehr 120 mm mortar (Tampella), M8.3a: range over 6 km (Bundeswehr page, search extract), total mass 160 kg, a round almost 14 kg; carried by the Wolf (G-Wagen) and fired from a baseplate, or from the M113 (search extracts). Minimum range 500 m, set-up 120 s, packing 60 s, a round every 8 s sustained, crew 4 (2 can still fire), first-round aim error 15 m, dispersion 8 m per km, processing 30 s, flight 10 s + 6 s per km and heard out to 4 km are game values (no public source for them found). The carrier is not modelled: the section starts at its position.

M9.4a (owner M9 round: one quadcopter at the platoon HQ): a MIKADO / AirRobot class quadcopter (search extracts: small electric quadcopter for day and night reconnaissance in close and built-up terrain, about 1,000 m range, carried by one soldier; the 2022 replacement folds and its backpack system weighs 15 kg). Which platoons have one is not public; mass, speeds, endurance (about 30 min) and camera values are game values.
M9.4a: the quadcopter's flight battery; charge in Wh (Mavic 3 class: 77 Wh; DE a game value). Three per drone (game value, low).

One half of the Bundeswehr Erkennungsmarke: an oval stainless-steel tag perforated across the middle, both halves stamped alike, so either half identifies the man; on his death one half is broken off for the formalities and the other stays with him (bundeswehr.de, search extract). Counted as two items per man (a whole tag = two halves). Mass about 10 g per half: not published, typical value (low).

One 120 mm DM63A1 cartridge (combustible case), a single-round magazine for the gun's feeds and the stowage (M7.6a). Cartridge mass is a game value. Mass (review fix): the item's own 16.8 kg is the case and propellant, its charge the 4.6 kg projectile (the ammunition's cartridgeMassKg), so a loaded round weighs the 21.4 kg cartridge, as the 9M131 splits tube and missile.

One 120 mm DM11 cartridge, a single-round magazine (M7.6a). Mass is a game value. Mass (review fix): the item's own 12.6 kg is the case and propellant, its charge the 11.4 kg projectile (the ammunition's cartridgeMassKg), so a loaded round weighs the 24.0 kg cartridge, as the 9M131 splits tube and missile.
250-round belt for the Leopard's coaxial MG3A1, every fifth round tracer (game values; 4750 rounds of 7.62 mm carried is the common figure, from memory).

The Leopard 2A7V's fuel tanks (M7.6a): the charge is litres of diesel (0.84 kg per litre); the tanks are part of the hull (mass 0). About 1160 L is the figure usually quoted (from memory, not in the extracts): game value.
Game value: one charge of the Leopard's fire suppression system (M7.6a).

100-round belt for the FLW 200's 12.7 mm machine gun: the station holds 100 ready rounds (KNDS listing, search extract, medium); nine more belts stowed in the hull (1,000 rounds in all) are a game value (low).

32-round belt in its box for the 40 mm GMW (M7.6d): the FLW 200 holds one box of 32 ready rounds (KNDS, Bundeswehr, search extracts, medium); a box of link and case of about 2 kg is a game value (low). The same box feeds the GMW on its tripod.

40 mm GMW on its ground tripod (M7.6d): gun 28.8 kg plus tripod 10.7 kg (Wikipedia, search extract, medium; the Bundeswehr page gives a 15 kg tripod: sources conflict). Carried by the team's gunner as one load here (in practice the team splits gun and tripod). The crewServed block: set-up 45 s, packing 20 s, crew 3 (Truppfuehrer, Richtschuetze, Ladeschuetze: Bundeswehr, medium), the fewest who can still fire 1, sight 0.9 m, traverse +-30 deg before a 5 s re-lay, 2 s to lay, engages men on its own out to 1500 m (HK's effective range, medium): game values otherwise (low).

M11.1: fourteen 10-round stripper clips in a cloth bandolier (140 rounds): the pattern of 5.56 x 45 mm packaging in seller listings of the military issue (search extracts, plan section 3); Bundeswehr packaging not found, assumed the same. Empty mass (cloth, clips) a game value. A man loads a magazine from it with clips (faster).

M11.1: six bandoliers (840 rounds) in a metal can (M2A1 pattern, seller listings via search extracts; Bundeswehr use assumed). Can mass about 2.4 kg (derived, game value). Carried forward to a supply point; men refill magazines from it.

M11.1: a can of 200 linked 7.62 x 51 mm rounds (US M19A1 pattern, about 1.7-1.8 kg empty, search extracts); the MG5 gunner loads 120-round belts, so a can's rounds go to belts out of battle (game). Bundeswehr packaging not found.
M11.1: a crate of 40 x 46 mm grenades for the AG36; the count per crate was not found (game value). Each round about 0.23 kg as the de-40mm-he round.
M11.1: a crate of DM51 hand grenades; the count per crate was not found (game value).
